360	Pesach, we learn the laws of Pesach. It is not an obligation that every rabbi
361	in his community
362	must expound for 30 days beforehand, begin to teach them the laws of
363	Pesach. It is not necessary.
364	It is not an obligation. What people do is a custom.
365	But what the Gemara says, "they ask about the laws of Pesach,"
366	does not mean that every sage sits and studies the laws of Pesach, or
367	every sage in the yeshiva or kollel sits and studies the laws of
368	Pesach. Even those who learn in the kollel have a
369	set study schedule, which is a different one. They continue in their own study and are not
370	obligated to stop in order to study the laws of Pesach. Rather,
371	what is "they ask about the laws of Pesach"? Look, Maran did not
372	write "they expound,"
373	but rather "they ask about the laws of Pesach before the Pesach of the festival."
374	What does "they ask" mean?
375	In the Tosefta, tractate Sanhedrin, it is written that when they
376	sat in the Beit HaVaad, as they called it, the Beit
377	HaVaad, the place where
378	the Torah scholars gathered, they would sit together and clarify
379	the laws. One would rise and ask the head of the Sanhedrin: What is the law
380	in such and such a matter? He answers him; one has to answer
381	him.
382	If someone disagrees, he tells him he has
383	arguments, let him state his arguments. But generally,
384	when there are no disputes, they continue, and learn all
385	the laws that they ask them, one after another, as the one asking.
386	But one must ask a matter in its proper time, not ask things
387	that are not relevant to the subject. If they are dealing with the laws of
388	Shabbat, and one gets up and asks about the laws of mourning, what does
389	mourning have to do with Shabbat? Why are you asking such questions? One
390	asks only about what they are engaged in.
391	"He asks on the subject and answers according to the halachah": if a person asks on that same
392	subject, they answer him according to the halachah. If not, it confuses
393	the rabbi, and instead of answering correctly, he answers him
394	incorrectly, because his whole mind, all his intellect, was focused
395	on the matters they were engaged in, and suddenly he takes
396	him to another place, so a mistake can come of it. Therefore
397	they ask only at that hour; he answers on the subject
398	and they rule according to the halachah. Therefore, if two asked, one
